question: Union of the epiphysis of the iliac crest is complete by 20–21 years of age and is therefore used as a skeletal marker to confirm that an individual has passed the age of majority (18 years).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The iliac crest epiphyseal union completes at 20–21 years — slightly later than the legal age of majority (18 years). An unfused iliac crest epiphysis therefore cannot confirm someone is over 18; full fusion does confirm age ≥20–21. This distinction is critical when estimating age in criminal cases involving juveniles.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The iliac crest epiphysis fuses at approximately 20–21 years. Because its fusion occurs after age 18, an unfused iliac crest epiphysis indicates the individual is likely below 21 years, and its presence (fully fused) confirms age ≥21. This makes it one of the most forensically significant epiphyseal markers in Indian practice.
